PullRequest.Title: Fixes #347108: open sessions and chats dropped on a chat window
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347108

### Repro
Drag a session row from the Sessions list in the main Agents window onto a chat window. Before the fix, no drop target accepted the drag: nothing opened in the chat window, and a drag over a long transcript scrolled it. A chat tab dragged from the main window had the same problem, and over the chat input only the "Attach Chat as Context" overlay was available.

### Root cause
Chat windows never implemented a drop target for sessions or chats. The paths named in the triage notes (`partGridDnd.ts`, `chatGroupDropTarget.ts`) are not involved.

### Fix
- Adds `ChatWindowSessionDropTarget`, wired from `ChatEditorView`. It accepts session-row and chat-tab drags and shows a fixed-position overlay over the transcript, sized from the chat view with a hole over the chat input. The overlay also suppresses the transcript auto-scroll during the drag.
- The drop opens the chat in that chat window through `IChatWindowService.open` (the existing path, no new API), as a tab at the drop position.
- Archived or gone chats show no indicator and do nothing on drop (a chat-tab drop re-checks at drop time).
- The "Attach Chat as Context" drop on the chat input is unchanged, and editor drags are not accepted by the new target.

### Known limit
A chat that is already shown in another chat window is revealed there rather than moved, matching link behavior. Moving between chat windows stays with the existing chat-tab drag. A chat in the main window's grid moves into the chat window.

### Tests
- New unit tests for the drop target (`chatWindowSessionDropTarget.test.ts`), including archived-chat and overlay geometry cases.
- New wiring test in `chatEditor.test.ts` driving `ChatEditorView` with a session drag. It fails with the pre-fix `chatEditor.ts` and passes with the fix.
- Both test files pass when run in isolation. Related chat window, sessions and editor DnD suites, typecheck, eslint and `valid-layers-check` were run.

### Live verification
Run in a Code - OSS Agents window copy.
- Before (unfixed `chatEditor.ts`): a session row dropped on a chat window with a long transcript shows no overlay and does not move.
- After: the overlay shows, and the dropped session opens as a second tab.
- Neighbors: a chat tab drop opens as an active tab; the input shows only the attach overlay and the hole leaves the input reachable; an editor tab drag shows no overlay; with two tabs the overlay starts below the tab strip.
- Limits: the dragstart and drop events were synthetic (CDP), so there was no native OS drag. Native Chromium autoscroll was not measured. Drop on the chat input and drag out were not run live.

### Review
An independent review on a different model ran the full matrix. Two findings (archived chat payload, overlay containing block) were repaired and the reviewer approved with no remaining findings.


### Cross-window session drop (review feedback)
A session row dragged from another top-level window has no entry in this renderer's local drag transfer, so the drop opened nothing. The drop now falls back to the typed session payload (`sessionId` and `resource`, both required to be strings; malformed or wrongly typed data is ignored). The resource is never opened directly: it must resolve to a session already known to the sessions management service, and archived or gone chats are still rejected.
- Red/green: the new unit test fails with the previous `chatWindowSessionDropTarget.ts` and passes with the fix; the chat window and chat editor suites and typecheck pass.
- Review: the same independent reviewer approved the delta with no findings, including payload trust (types, unknown resource, archived chat, another workspace or host).
- Live: the Agents window is a single top-level window, so a drag from a second Agents window could not be run live (not run). Instead, a session row was dropped onto a chat window with no local drag transfer, which exercises the typed-payload path: the overlay shows and the chat opens as the active tab. The same-window drag behaves as before. The dragstart and drop were synthetic (CDP).
- Known limit: for payloads that cannot be read before the drop (cross-window sessions and chat tabs), the indicator is provisional. An unknown or archived one may show the indicator and then do nothing on drop.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The sessions list explicitly enables multiple selection and stores every selected row in `DraggedSessionIdentifier[]`; the changed loop consumes that full array. The concrete `getSession` implementation creates the merged provider-session array and performs a linear URI search per call, so the K-by-N scaling and its execution inside the drop event are directly traced. Exact wall-clock magnitude depends on catalog size and URI/provider costs.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, URI comparisons, and repeatedly allocated merged-session arrays
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For K dragged sessions and N sessions across providers, resolution is O(K*N) and allocates K merged arrays; selecting most of an N-row list makes the pre-open work O(N^2).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked UI-thread drop handling and increased CPU/GC pressure before chat opening begins
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Chat windows did not accept session-list drops, so this synchronous multi-selection resolution path and its repeated full-catalog work did not run.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new chat-window drop target resolves every locally selected session separately and synchronously before starting the asynchronous chat-opening loop.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 154 places `_resolveSessionChat(item.resource)` inside the loop over every dragged session; `_resolveSessionChat` calls `ISessionsManagementService.getSession`, whose implementation rebuilds `_getMergedSessions()` and linearly searches it on every call.
Findings.Title: Resolve multi-selected sessions from one catalog snapshot
Findings.Impact: Shift/Ctrl-selecting a large set of sessions and dropping it on a chat window can freeze the UI after the drop and delay the first tab opening while the renderer performs repeated catalog scans and allocations.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionsListDragAndDrop.onDragStart` maps all selected sessions into the local transfer, and `multipleSelectionSupport` is true. `_handleDrop` then loops over that array and calls `_resolveSessionChat` for each item. `_resolveSessionChat` calls `getSession`; `SessionsManagementService.getSession` invokes `_getMergedSessions()` and `.find(...)` each time. Thus selecting K rows from N sessions causes K full catalog constructions/scans (quadratic when selecting most rows), plus per-session archive checks, synchronously in the DOM drop handler.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve local multi-selection from one `getSessions()` snapshot indexed by current resource (preserving drag order and the existing archived/gone checks), rather than calling `getSession` per item; retain a single-item lookup only for payload cases that cannot come from that snapshot.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag one or many session rows from the main Sessions list onto an existing chat window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On `dragenter`, acceptance and one geometry/clip-path calculation must finish before the indicator appears. On drop, all selected sessions are synchronously resolved and checked before the asynchronous opening loop starts, so the reported O(K*N) work blocks the first tab and the next paint. Each subsequent chat open is awaited in order.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM geometry and append/style a fixed overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `getBoundingClientRect` for the chat plus clip-path geometry for contained registered inputs when the accepted drag first enters; not repeated on dragover.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat-window session/chat overlay or geometry work ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous browser layout reads delay indicator display once, but are bounded and did not establish a separate regression.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each chat through the sessions chat-window provider and open its editor in the target chat window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K in-process opens for K valid selected sessions, one after another; each resolves the chat and opens an editor tab. Same-chat requests are coalesced, but normal multi-selection contains unique chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dropping sessions on a chat window opened zero chats. Existing non-chat-window drop paths use their own batched session operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first open is blocked by synchronous session resolution for all K items; later opens determine completion of the full multi-tab operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K selected live session rows out of N total provider sessions; K can approach N via range/select-all style multi-selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session resolution is fully synchronous. Chat opens are intentionally serialized by the changed `for`/`await` loop; the service also sequences same-chat opens by key, while distinct chats would otherwise be independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The drag payload and local transfer are already populated; overlay geometry is not cached but is computed only when the overlay is first shown. Session lookup has no per-drop snapshot/cache: each selected resource rebuilds and scans the merged provider catalog. Chat-window `open` coalesces the same exact chat in flight, but distinct selected chats do not share resolution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: multi-selection is enabled, all selected rows are transferred, the changed loop calls `getSession` per row, and `getSession` rebuilds and linearly scans the complete merged catalog.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on provider count, session count, URI comparison cost, and how often users drag large selections; the quadratic synchronous mechanism is certain, so magnitude affects severity rather than confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression for large local multi-selections: session resolution is O(K*N) on the UI-thread drop path. Single-row drops remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop a session row originating in another top-level window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provisional overlay is shown from the MIME type. On drop, JSON parsing, one session lookup/archive check, and one in-process chat open are on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse typed drag data, validate it against known sessions, and open the resolved main chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-process chat resolution/editor open per cross-window drop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the dropped chat appears; bounded to one.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One typed session payload; cross-window data transfer does not carry the full local multi-selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one payload item is accepted cross-window, so one open runs; no fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cross-window typed payload contains only the first session and is parsed once on drop. Session lookup uses the current management-service state; there is no negative cache, but the operation is not repeated during dragover. Existing chat-open in-flight coalescing applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the payload reader constructs a one-element array and the drop path validates it before opening.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-side session lookup cost varies with catalog size, but there is only one lookup and one open.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: work is bounded to one lookup/open and adds no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag a chat tab from the main window onto a chat-window transcript.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One session/chat ownership scan and one editor open/reveal must complete before the tab appears. Overlay geometry is computed once on entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the dragged chat, then resolve and open/reveal it in the target window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat-window transcript did not accept this tab drop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the tab to open or reveal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dragged chat tab and the size of the in-memory session catalog used for ownership lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One chat per tab drag; no fan-out or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat-tab drag data names one chat. The service reuses/reveals an already-open chat and coalesces an identical in-flight open; otherwise the provider resolves it against current in-memory sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `getSessionChatDragData` selects the single-chat branch and bypasses the selected-session loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat/editor construction cost varies, but cardinality is fixed at one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one bounded open is intrinsic to the feature, is coalesced when already in flight, and no new external I/O boundary was found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag files, editors, or a chat reference over the chat input rather than the transcript.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MIME/type checks and registered-input hit testing decide rejection before any open. No changed subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One drag event; unrelated file/editor payloads are rejected.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No overlay or lookup is created for unrelated drags; input attachment drops retain their existing nested target behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; rejection is constant/bounded except existing registered-target traversal for input hit testing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the new target does not create an overlay or open chats for these paths, and existing input handling remains authoritative.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced drag-enter, local/cross-window drop, chat-tab open, overlay cleanup, geometry/layout, session lookup, and chat-window open paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-high repeated-work finding for synchronous O(K*N) multi-selection resolution; no external subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundaries were introduced.
